title: The dispatch role refuses a candidate whose CoS it cannot check
action:
Per D4 (store b03574c6). In skills/bee-herding/references/role-dispatch.md, extend the existing two-key lane-safety filter — Key 2 at :273 already says 'Read the candidate's full title+cos yourself', so this is a SECOND question over text the role already has in hand, not a new read.

Add the rule: a candidate whose Condition of Satisfaction is not CHECKABLE is skipped, and the skip line NAMES why. Checkable means the CoS points at something an agent can evaluate — a command it can run, a file:line it can open, or a repository state it can inspect. It is a reading rule, not a regex: do not add a keyword list.

Carry a worked pair so the rule is teachable rather than abstract:
- NOT checkable — `cos: "make the parser better"`. Nothing to run, nothing to open, no state to compare. Skip line: `SKIPPED p-xxxxxxxx — cos is not checkable: it names no command, path, or state an agent can evaluate.`
- Checkable — `cos: "zero old callers remain and every parser fixture passes"`. Two evaluable facts.

State the boundary plainly in one line: this fires at DISPATCH time only. Nothing checks a CoS when it is written, so a vague item is accepted at filing and refused later, with its author out of the loop — that gap is filed as backlog p-0b2812f8 and is deliberately NOT closed here.

Run `bee dev regen` after touching skills/**.
acceptance: role-dispatch.md's lane-safety filter carries the checkable-CoS rule, a worked checkable/uncheckable pair, the exact skip-line wording, and the one-line statement that authoring-time checking is out of scope with its backlog id. No keyword list was added. release-manifest --check passes after regen.
